outcome_tree.root_description: Estratégia aplicada ao estado clínico inicial: Radioterapia externa selecionada

outcomes.label: response_control
outcomes.description: A radioterapia externa selecionada resultou em controle locorregional, sem evidência de progressão radiológica após 12 meses de seguimento.
outcomes.mechanism: A radioterapia foi bem planejada e aplicada, resultando em controle da doença locorregional.
modifiers: A paciente não apresentou toxicidade significativa durante o tratamento.

outcomes.label: recurrence_progression
outcomes.description: A radioterapia externa selecionada não conseguiu controlar a progressão radiológica da doença metastática pulmonar, com evidência de crescimento tumoral após 6 meses de seguimento.
outcomes.mechanism: A radioterapia foi aplicada conforme protocolo, mas a doença metastática pulmonar persistiu e progrediu.
modifiers: A paciente apresentou toxicidade moderada durante o tratamento.

outcomes.label: toxicity
outcomes.description: A radioterapia externa selecionada resultou em toxicidade cervical moderada, com disfagia e dermatite após 3 meses de tratamento.
outcomes.mechanism: A radioterapia foi bem planejada, mas a dose aplicada causou toxicidade cervical moderada.
modifiers: A paciente apresentou melhora gradual da toxicidade após ajuste da dose.

outcomes.label: quality_of_life
outcomes.description: A radioterapia externa selecionada manteve a qualidade de vida da paciente, sem comprometer atividades de vida diária.
outcomes.mechanism: A radioterapia foi bem tolerada e não causou sintomas significativos que afetassem a qualidade de vida.
modifiers: A paciente relatou leve dispneia aos grandes esforços, mas não foi afetada em suas atividades diárias.

outcomes.label: mortality
outcomes.description: A radioterapia externa selecionada não foi capaz de alterar o curso da doença, resultando em morte da paciente após 18 meses de seguimento.
outcomes.mechanism: A radioterapia foi aplicada conforme protocolo, mas não foi suficiente para controlar a progressão da doença metastática.
modifiers: A paciente desenvolveu complicações cardiovasculares graves após 12 meses de seguimento.

outcome_tree.root_description: Estratégia aplicada ao estado clínico inicial: Inibidor multiquinase para doença refratária ao radioiodo

outcomes.label: response_control
outcomes.description: A paciente respondeu favoravelmente ao tratamento, mantendo controle da doença progressiva refratária ao radioiodo. A radiological_progression foi estabilizada e a tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido retornou ao normal. A paciente não apresentou toxicidades significativas.
outcomes.mechanism: A inibição multiquinase foi eficaz em inibir os mecanismos de progressão da doença refratária ao radioiodo.

outcomes.label: persistence
outcomes.description: A paciente manteve a doença progressiva refratária ao radioiodo, com estabilização da radiological_progression. No entanto, a tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido permaneceu elevada. A paciente apresentou hipertensão leve, controlada com ajuste da losartana.
outcomes.mechanism: A inibição multiquinase foi capaz de estabilizar a progressão da doença, mas não foi suficiente para induzir uma resposta completa.
modifiers: hipertensão leve

outcomes.label: recurrence_progression
outcomes.description: A paciente apresentou recorrência progressiva da doença refratária ao radioiodo, com radiological_progression documentada. A tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido aumentou significativamente. A paciente desenvolveu diarreia moderada, que foi bem controlada.
outcomes.mechanism: A inibição multiquinase não foi capaz de controlar a progressão da doença refratária ao radioiodo.
modifiers: diarreia moderada

outcomes.label: toxicity
outcomes.description: A paciente apresentou toxicidades significativas, incluindo hipertensão moderada e fadiga severa. A tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido aumentou. A paciente não apresentou controle da doença progressiva refratária ao radioiodo.
outcomes.mechanism: A inibição multiquinase foi capaz de induzir toxicidades significativas, prejudicando o controle da doença.
modifiers: hipertensão moderada
fadiga severa

outcomes.label: quality_of_life
outcomes.description: A paciente relatou uma qualidade de vida significativamente afetada devido à progressão da doença refratária ao radioiodo. A tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido aumentou. A paciente não apresentou controle da doença progressiva refratária ao radioiodo.
outcomes.mechanism: A inibição multiquinase não foi capaz de controlar a progressão da doença refratária ao radioiodo, prejudicando a qualidade de vida da paciente.
modifiers: progressão da doença refratária ao radioiodo

outcomes.label: subsequent_therapy
outcomes.description: A paciente necessitou de terapia subsequente devido à progressão da doença refratária ao radioiodo. A tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido aumentou. A paciente não apresentou controle da doença progressiva refratária ao radioiodo.
outcomes.mechanism: A inibição multiquinase não foi capaz de controlar a progressão da doença refratária ao radioiodo, levando à necessidade de terapia subsequente.

external_evidence.finding: regimen due to its higher response rate and longer PFS compared to sorafenib in these landmark studies. Clinical interpretation. The results of prospective, ran- domized, placebo-controlled studies conﬁrm the beneﬁt o f treatment with multikinase TKIs in patients with RAI- refractory, well-differentiated thyroid cancer. Most pa- tients who require treatment for their disease are symp- tomatic and need a reduction in tumor burden. Since the response rates for lenvatinib are almost three times that of sorafenib, lenvatinib is generally the preferred ﬁrst-line agent. Similarly, PFS is longer with lenvatinib. However, head-to-head studies comparing the efﬁcacy of these two agents are lacking. Both lenvatinib and sorafenib were as- sociated with signiﬁcant adverse effects that often led to dose reductions and discontinuation of therapy in their respective randomized, placebo-controlled trials. In general, sorafenib is associated with increased hand-foot skin re- actions and diarrhea. Lenvatinib, on the other hand, causes more frequent hypertension, weight loss, and proteinuria.

guideline_evidence.finding: regimen due to its higher response rate and longer PFS compared to sorafenib in these landmark studies. Clinical interpretation. The results of prospective, ran- domized, placebo-controlled studies conﬁrm the beneﬁt o f treatment with multikinase TKIs in patients with RAI- refractory, well-differentiated thyroid cancer. Most pa- tients who require treatment for their disease are symp- tomatic and need a reduction in tumor burden. Since the response rates for lenvatinib are almost three times that of sorafenib, lenvatinib is generally the preferred ﬁrst-line agent. Similarly, PFS is longer with lenvatinib. However, head-to-head studies comparing the efﬁcacy of these two agents are lacking. Both lenvatinib and sorafenib were as- sociated with signiﬁcant adverse effects that often led to dose reductions and discontinuation of therapy in their respective randomized, placebo-controlled trials. In general, sorafenib is associated with increased hand-foot skin re- actions and diarrhea. Lenvatinib, on the other hand, causes more frequent hypertension, weight loss, and proteinuria.

outcomes.label: response_control

modifiers: Controle da tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido.

outcomes.label: recurrence_progression

outcomes.mechanism: Progressão radiológica da doença metastática pulmonar e deterioração da qualidade de vida.
modifiers: Aumento da tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido.
Dispneia intensificada.

outcomes.label: toxicity

outcomes.mechanism: Toxicidade moderada da losartana e deterioração da qualidade de vida.
modifiers: Aumento da pressão arterial sistólica.
Dispneia intensificada.

modifiers: Controle da tireoglobulina sob TSH suprimido.
Pressão arterial sistólica controlada.

outcome.label: progression
outcome.description: A progressão radiológica da doença metastática pulmonar continuou, resultando em um aumento significativo do tamanho das metástases pulmonares detectadas por tomografia computadorizada (CT).

parent.hypothesis: A hipertensão arterial pode ter contribuído para a progressão da doença metastática pulmonar.
parent.mechanism: A hipertensão arterial pode ter aumentado a pressão arterial sistólica, levando a um aumento da perfusão pulmonar e, consequentemente, ao crescimento das metástases pulmonares.

external_evidence.finding: best practices for prevention, screening, palliative and supportive care, and disease management of cancer. In the United States, many patients remain unable to reap the beneﬁts of innovative prevention and early detection programs, biomarker testing, and new cancer therapies due to challenges including lack of transportation, stable housing, adequate insurance coverage, food insecurity, health literacy, proximity to a dedicated cancer center, and cost of treatment and other services. 94 Additionally, some populations experience stigma along with barriers to cancer screening, prevention, and treatment that contribute to these cancer disparities. 95 Further, geographic disparities can also impact the quality- of-care patients receive. Rural patients are more likely to have worse survivorship outcomes and experience higher mortality rates compared to nonrural patients. This can be attributed, in part, to a lower density of specialists and dedicated cancer centers, as only 21% of nonmetropolitan counties in the United States have one or more practicing oncologists.
external_evidence.relevance: 5 termos da consulta correspondem ao trecho.

external_evidence.finding: Furthermore, access to the necessary systemic therapy medications, including MKIs, may vary based on treatment location. Finally, many thyroid malignancies are rare; expertise in management is not universal and may impact care. Overall, there is signiﬁcant opportunity to improve access to swift diagnosis, high-quality pathological diagnosis, and expertise in multidisciplinary treatment of thyroid carci- nomas to improve patient care. MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS Creating evidence-based recommendations to inform treat- ment of patients with additional chronic conditions, a situa- tion in which the patient may have two or more such conditions—referred to as multiple chronic conditions (MCC)—is challenging. Patients with MCC are a complex and heterogeneous population, making it difﬁcult to account for all of the possible permutations to develop speciﬁc recommen- dations for care. In addition, the best available evidence for treating index conditions, such as cancer, is often from clinical trials whose study selection criteria may exclude these patients in order to avoid potential interaction effects or confounding of results associated with MCC.
external_evidence.relevance: 5 termos da consulta correspondem ao trecho.

external_evidence.finding: While other MKIs may be con- sidered as second-line therapy, cabozantinib is the pre- ferred agent since COSMIC-311 is the only published randomized study demonstrating clinical beneﬁt. Hyper- tension, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, and fatigue are the most common side effects associated with cabo- zantinib, all of which are manageable with supportive care, dose holding, and reductions. Preexisting, poorly con- trolled hypertension, or renal dysfunction may preclude its use due to concerns for developing cardiovascular disease and proteinuria. Question 2 In patients with RAI-refractory, well-differentiated thyroid cancer (papillary, follicular, oncocytic), do genomically targeted therapies compared to placebo or observation impact survival and what should be recommended in the ﬁrst-line and subsequent-line setting? Recommendation 2.1 Literature review and analysis. Genomic testing should be performed to evaluate alterations that may confer beneﬁt from a personalized treatment strategy with targeted therapies.

guideline_evidence.finding: While other MKIs may be con- sidered as second-line therapy, cabozantinib is the pre- ferred agent since COSMIC-311 is the only published randomized study demonstrating clinical beneﬁt. Hyper- tension, palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, and fatigue are the most common side effects associated with cabo- zantinib, all of which are manageable with supportive care, dose holding, and reductions. Preexisting, poorly con- trolled hypertension, or renal dysfunction may preclude its use due to concerns for developing cardiovascular disease and proteinuria. Question 2 In patients with RAI-refractory, well-differentiated thyroid cancer (papillary, follicular, oncocytic), do genomically targeted therapies compared to placebo or observation impact survival and what should be recommended in the ﬁrst-line and subsequent-line setting? Recommendation 2.1 Literature review and analysis. Genomic testing should be performed to evaluate alterations that may confer beneﬁt from a personalized treatment strategy with targeted therapies.

guideline_evidence.finding: best practices for prevention, screening, palliative and supportive care, and disease management of cancer. In the United States, many patients remain unable to reap the beneﬁts of innovative prevention and early detection programs, biomarker testing, and new cancer therapies due to challenges including lack of transportation, stable housing, adequate insurance coverage, food insecurity, health literacy, proximity to a dedicated cancer center, and cost of treatment and other services. 94 Additionally, some populations experience stigma along with barriers to cancer screening, prevention, and treatment that contribute to these cancer disparities. 95 Further, geographic disparities can also impact the quality- of-care patients receive. Rural patients are more likely to have worse survivorship outcomes and experience higher mortality rates compared to nonrural patients. This can be attributed, in part, to a lower density of specialists and dedicated cancer centers, as only 21% of nonmetropolitan counties in the United States have one or more practicing oncologists.

guideline_evidence.finding: Furthermore, access to the necessary systemic therapy medications, including MKIs, may vary based on treatment location. Finally, many thyroid malignancies are rare; expertise in management is not universal and may impact care. Overall, there is signiﬁcant opportunity to improve access to swift diagnosis, high-quality pathological diagnosis, and expertise in multidisciplinary treatment of thyroid carci- nomas to improve patient care. MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS Creating evidence-based recommendations to inform treat- ment of patients with additional chronic conditions, a situa- tion in which the patient may have two or more such conditions—referred to as multiple chronic conditions (MCC)—is challenging. Patients with MCC are a complex and heterogeneous population, making it difﬁcult to account for all of the possible permutations to develop speciﬁc recommen- dations for care. In addition, the best available evidence for treating index conditions, such as cancer, is often from clinical trials whose study selection criteria may exclude these patients in order to avoid potential interaction effects or confounding of results associated with MCC.
